There they will place the most holy things—the offering, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance—for the place is holy.

target_units.text: And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

initial_triples.relationship: close holy priestly chambers and preparation of their offerings
initial_triples.rationale: The source assigns northern and southern holy chambers to priests for eating and placing the holy offerings. The later vision leads into a northern priestly chamber and identifies the place for boiling sin and ignorance offerings and baking the grain offering. The later preparation instructions add a specific function to the chamber-and-offering connection.
initial_triples.source_text: He said to me, “The recessed chambers toward the north and toward the south, facing the intervening spaces, are the chambers of the holy place. There the priests, the sons of Zadok who draw near to the Lord, will eat the most holy things. There they will place the most holy things—the offering, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance—for the place is holy.

target_units.text: He brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the north-facing recessed chamber of the priests’ holy places. Look—there was a separated place there.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the offerings for ignorance and for sin, and there bake the entire grain offering, so as not to carry it out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”

initial_triples.relationship: close change of holy ministry garments before contact with the people
initial_triples.rationale: The source requires other garments when the priests come into contact with the people, preserving the holiness of ministry garments. The later instruction explicitly places those robes in holy chambers and requires different robes in the outer court. Its statement about not sanctifying the people is preserved as its own formulation.
initial_triples.source_text: No one will enter there except the priests. They will not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that those who bring offerings may always be holy and may not touch the garments in which they minister, for they are holy. They will put on other garments whenever they come into contact with the people.”

target_units.text: When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the robes in which they minister, place them in the recessed chambers of the holy places, and put on other robes. They will certainly not sanctify the people with their robes.

initial_triples.relationship: related architectural separation involving holy space
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's measured enclosure distinguishes the holy areas from the forewall in the house's arrangement. Exodus uses a veil to distinguish the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies. Both give an architectural boundary a separating role, but the source's forewall is not renamed profane space and the two boundaries separate different areas.
initial_triples.source_text: The four sides were measured with the same reed. He laid it out, with their enclosure all around: five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to distinguish between the holy areas and the forewall in the arrangement of the house.

target_units.text: And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

initial_triples.relationship: related sound and radiance accompanying the Lord's glory
initial_triples.rationale: The arriving glory is accompanied by the sound of a camp like many redoubling their sound, and the earth flashes with radiance. The earlier vision combines wing-sound like much water with surrounding brightness and the appearance of the Lord's glory. The distinct sound comparisons are preserved; this source does not itself say many waters.
initial_triples.source_text: Look—the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way of the gate facing east. The sound of the camp was like the sound of many redoubling their sound, and the earth flashed like radiance from the glory all around.

target_units.text: As they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water; when they stood, their wings came to rest.
And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads.
Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.

Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.

initial_triples.relationship: close recollection of the river vision and falling on the face
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel compares the present vision with the one at the River Chobar and falls on his face. His earlier plain encounter likewise recalled the glory seen by the river and included falling on his face. The source's separate phrase about entering to anoint the city is not changed to destroying it.
initial_triples.source_text: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I was entering to anoint the city; and the vision of the chariot I saw was like the vision I had seen by the River Chobar. I fall on my face.

target_units.text: I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.

initial_triples.relationship: related reversal between the glory's departure and entrance
initial_triples.rationale: The glory now enters the house through the east-facing gate. In the earlier scene it departed from the house and rose upon the cherubim, who stood at the opposite gate. The inward and outward movements are the connection; the target's gate is not silently renamed east-facing.
initial_triples.source_text: The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.

target_units.text: The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.

initial_triples.relationship: close divine glory filling the sanctuary
initial_triples.rationale: After a spirit lifts Ezekiel into the inner court, he sees the house full of the Lord's glory. Exodus describes the tent filled with that glory, so that Moses cannot enter. The sanctuary-filling manifestation is shared while the buildings and human movements differ.
initial_triples.source_text: A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.

target_units.text: The cloud covered the Tent of Testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Moses could not enter the Tent of Testimony because the cloud overshadowed it and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.

initial_triples.relationship: close divine glory filling the house
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel sees the house full of the Lord's glory. At Solomon's dedication the cloud fills the house and the priests cannot stand to minister because the Lord's glory fills it. This links the same stated house-filling presence across distinct scenes.
initial_triples.source_text: A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.

target_units.text: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the Lord’s glory filled the house.

initial_triples.relationship: related divine speech heard from the sanctuary
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel hears a voice from the house while the guiding man stands beside him. Moses likewise hears the Lord's voice from within the Tent of Testimony, there specified as above the ark's cover between the cherubim. The common sanctuary setting does not identify Ezekiel's companion with the speaking voice.
initial_triples.source_text: I stood, and look—a voice from the house, speaking to me, while the man stood next to me.

target_units.text: When Moses entered the Tent of Testimony to speak with Him, he heard the voice of the Lord speaking to him from above the propitiatory cover on the ark of Testimony, between the two cherubim. He spoke to him.

initial_triples.relationship: close description of the sanctuary as a place for God's feet
initial_triples.rationale: God identifies the place of His throne and the footprints of His feet. David likewise describes his intended sanctuary as a standing place for the Lord's feet and a house of rest for the ark. The feet-and-dwelling language is shared without adding the source's throne to David's statement.
initial_triples.source_text: He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man, the place of My throne and the place of the footprints of My feet, where My name will dwell among the house of Israel for ever? The house of Israel will no longer profane My holy name, neither they nor their rulers, by their prostitution and by the murders of the rulers among them—

target_units.text: David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, “Hear me, brethren and my people. It came upon my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the Lord’s covenant and a standing place for our Lord’s feet, and I prepared the things suitable for the dwelling.

initial_triples.relationship: close association of the divine name with the sanctuary
initial_triples.rationale: God says His name will dwell among Israel for ever in the place being shown. Solomon's account repeatedly identifies the chosen house as built for the Lord's name. The source's additional condemnation of prostitution and murders of rulers remains its own wording.
initial_triples.source_text: He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man, the place of My throne and the place of the footprints of My feet, where My name will dwell among the house of Israel for ever? The house of Israel will no longer profane My holy name, neither they nor their rulers, by their prostitution and by the murders of the rulers among them—

target_units.text: ‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city in any tribe of Israel in which to build a house for My name to be there; but I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there, and I chose David to be over My people Israel.’
It came into the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
But the Lord said to my father David, ‘Because it came into your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it came into your heart.
Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; your son who comes from your sides shall build the house for My name.’

The Lord has established the word He spoke. I have risen in place of my father David and sat on Israel’s throne, as the Lord promised, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.

initial_triples.relationship: related profanation of the divine dwelling by adjacent or inserted structures
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel condemns vestibules, doorposts and an adjoining wall associated with lawless deeds that profane God's name. Kings describes Manasseh placing rival altars and a carved image in the house where God placed His name. These are different spatial arrangements, connected by intrusion into the divine dwelling and dishonor to His name.
initial_triples.source_text: —when they set My vestibule among their vestibules and My doorposts next to their doorposts, and placed My wall as adjoining Me and them. They profaned My holy name by the lawless deeds they practiced, and I wiped them out in My wrath and in slaughter.

target_units.text: He built an altar in the Lord’s house, as He had said, ‘In Jerusalem I shall place My name.’
He built an altar for all heaven’s host in the two courts of the Lord’s house.
He led his sons through fire, practiced divination from sounds, read omens, and appointed a charmer and knowing ones. He did much evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.

He placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David and his son Solomon, ‘In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all Israel’s tribes, I shall place My name there for ever.

initial_triples.relationship: related removal of defilement and promised divine dwelling
initial_triples.rationale: God commands removal of prostitution and the murders of rulers and promises to dwell among the people. Paul likewise joins God's promised dwelling with separation from uncleanness and the incompatibility of God's temple with idols. The particular wrongs named in Ezekiel are not replaced by a claim about royal corpses.
initial_triples.source_text: Now let them drive their prostitution and the murders of their rulers away from Me, and I will dwell among them for ever.

target_units.text: And what agreement is there between God’s temple and idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Therefore come out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and do not touch anything unclean; and I will receive you.

initial_triples.relationship: related showing of the sanctuary's appearance and arrangement
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel must show the house and its arrangement to Israel, with the stated result that they cease from sins. Exodus likewise requires a sanctuary made according to the pattern God shows on the mountain. The acts of showing a sacred plan connect them, while the source's moral purpose differs from the target's construction command.
initial_triples.source_text: You, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, and they will cease from their sins. Show its appearance and its arrangement—

target_units.text: And you shall make it for Me according to all that I show you upon the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels; this is how you shall make it.

initial_triples.relationship: close recorded plans for sanctuary structure and ministry
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel must draw the house, its exits and structure, and make its commands and ordinances known. David likewise gives Solomon written patterns for the temple, surrounding chambers and ministry arrangements, received from the Lord's hand. The shared plans and service instructions do not equate their individual layouts.
initial_triples.source_text: —and they will receive their punishment for everything they have done. You will draw the house, its exits, and its structure; make known to them all its commands and all its ordinances, and draw them before them. They will keep all My judgments and all My commands and carry them out,

target_units.text: David gave Solomon his son the pattern of the temple, its houses, its zakcho, its upper rooms, its inner storerooms, and the house of propitiation;
and the pattern he had in his spirit: the courts of the Lord’s house, all the surrounding chambers for the storerooms of the Lord’s house, and the storerooms of the holy things;
and the lodgings of the priests’ and Levites’ service courses for all the work of ministry in the Lord’s house, and the storerooms of the service vessels for worship in the Lord’s house.
He gave the measure of their weight, both the gold and the silver ones;
he gave him the weight of the lampstands and of the lamps.
Likewise he gave him the weight of the tables of presentation, each golden table, and likewise of the silver ones;
and of the meat hooks, libation vessels, and golden bowls, and the weight of the gold and silver ones, kephphoure of each weight.
He showed him the weight of the incense altar of tested gold, and the pattern of the chariot of the cherubim with outspread wings, overshadowing the ark of the Lord’s covenant.
David gave Solomon everything in writing from the Lord’s hand, according to the understanding that had come to him about carrying out the pattern.

initial_triples.relationship: close designation of the sanctuary and surrounding land as holy
initial_triples.rationale: The house's drawing is on the mountain summit, and all its boundaries are most holy. The later land allocation likewise sets apart a holy portion with a sanctuary called the most holy place. The different extents and degrees of holiness are preserved rather than made into one identical boundary description.
initial_triples.source_text: together with the drawing of the house on the mountain’s summit: all its boundaries all around are most holy.”

target_units.text: “When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.
From this, a square of five hundred by five hundred will be for a sanctuary, with an interval of fifty cubits all around it.
From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.

initial_triples.relationship: close cubit-and-handbreadth convention in the vision's measurements
initial_triples.rationale: The altar account specifies a cubit consisting of a cubit and handbreadth. The earlier enclosing-wall measurement uses the same specified cubit within a six-cubit reed. The shared convention does not make the altar's ledge or hollow equal to the outer wall.
initial_triples.source_text: These are the altar’s measurements in a cubit consisting of a cubit and a handbreadth: a hollow one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a ledge along its edge all around of a span. This was the altar’s height:

target_units.text: Behold, an enclosure surrounded the house outside. In the man’s hand was a reed measuring six cubits by the cubit and handbreadth. He measured the outer wall: its width equaled the reed, and its height equaled the reed.

initial_triples.relationship: related altar access provisions with differing statements about steps
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's measured place of atonement has steps facing east. Exodus forbids ascending God's altar by steps, explaining this in terms of exposed nakedness. The two actual access provisions are compared without changing the source's steps into a ramp or declaring the instructions identical.
initial_triples.source_text: The place of atonement was fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its surrounding ledge ran all around it at half a cubit, and its surrounding band was a cubit all around. Its steps faced east.

target_units.text: You shall not go up by steps to My altar, lest you uncover your nakedness on it.’”

initial_triples.relationship: close burnt offerings and blood poured against the altar
initial_triples.rationale: The source introduces commands for offering burnt offerings and pouring blood against the altar when it is made. Exodus's priestly consecration instructions likewise pour a ram's blood against the altar and offer the ram as a whole burnt offering. The connection is the joined altar actions, not identical dedicatory timetables.
initial_triples.source_text: He said to me, “Son of man, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: These are the altar’s commands on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and pouring blood against it.

target_units.text: Slaughter it, take the blood, and pour it against the altar on every side.
Divide the ram limb by limb, wash the entrails and feet with water, and place them on the pieces with the head.
Offer the whole ram on the altar as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, a fragrant aroma; it is a sacrifice to the Lord.

initial_triples.relationship: close calf sin offering in the consecration of priests and altar
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns a calf sin offering to the Zadokite priests who draw near to minister. Leviticus describes Aaron and his sons with the calf sin offering, whose blood Moses uses to cleanse the altar. The offering and consecratory setting connect them without equating the named priestly groups.
initial_triples.source_text: You will give the Levitical priests who are of Zadok’s offspring and draw near to Me to minister to Me, says the Lord God, a calf from the cattle as an offering for sin.

target_units.text: And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.

initial_triples.relationship: close altar atonement through blood on horns and base
initial_triples.rationale: The priests apply blood to the altar's horns, the place of atonement's corners and the base, making atonement for it. Moses likewise applies calf blood to the altar's horns and pours it at the base to cleanse and consecrate it. The source's additional corners are not supplied by the target.
initial_triples.source_text: They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.

target_units.text: And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.

initial_triples.relationship: close burning of the calf sin offering outside the holy area
initial_triples.rationale: The sin-offering calf is burned in the house's separated area outside the holy places. Exodus likewise burns the sin-offering calf's flesh, skin and dung outside the camp. The removal and burning correspond while the source's sanctuary precinct and the target's camp remain distinct boundaries.
initial_triples.source_text: They will take the calf for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the separated area of the house, outside the holy places.

target_units.text: Burn the calf’s flesh, skin, and dung with fire outside the camp, for it is a sin offering.

initial_triples.relationship: related unblemished goats used as sin offerings
initial_triples.rationale: The second day requires two unblemished goat kids for sin and atonement for the altar. Leviticus requires an unblemished male young goat for a ruler's sin, applies blood to the altar and makes atonement for him. The animals and blood rite connect them without equating the number, occasion or object of atonement.
initial_triples.source_text: On the second day they will take two unblemished goat kids for sin, and they will make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the calf.

target_units.text: and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring as his gift an unblemished male young goat from the goats.
And he shall lay his hand upon the young goat’s head; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And he shall offer up all its fat upon the altar, as the fat of a sacrifice of deliverance. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

initial_triples.relationship: related cattle and unblemished rams in consecratory instructions
initial_triples.rationale: After the atonement, Ezekiel's instructions call for an unblemished calf and ram. Exodus's priestly consecration instructions likewise name a calf and unblemished rams, there two rams. The shared animal types and consecratory setting do not erase the stated numbers.
initial_triples.source_text: After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.

target_units.text: “This is what you shall do for them: consecrate them to serve Me as priests. Take one calf from the herd and two rams without blemish,

initial_triples.relationship: close requirement to add salt to offerings
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel's priests throw salt upon the animals before offering them as burnt offerings. Leviticus commands salt with every sacrificial gift and names the salt of the covenant. The salt requirement is shared; the target's covenant expression is not supplied as a quotation from Ezekiel.
initial_triples.source_text: You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.

target_units.text: And every gift of your sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of the Lord cease from your sacrifices; with every gift of yours you shall bring salt unto the Lord your God.

initial_triples.relationship: close seven-day consecratory offering prescriptions
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel specifies seven days of offerings, including a kid for sin each day and unblemished cattle and a ram. Exodus likewise orders seven days for consecration and altar purification and names the calf for sin. The seven-day framework connects them while the different animal lists remain distinct.
initial_triples.source_text: For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—

target_units.text: Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.
And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.

initial_triples.relationship: close seven-day altar purification and consecration of hands
initial_triples.rationale: The source requires seven days of atoning for and cleansing the altar and filling the priests' hands. Exodus likewise joins seven days of consecrating hands with seven days of purifying and consecrating the altar. The parallel concerns these joined consecratory actions rather than a merely repeated number.
initial_triples.source_text: —for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.

target_units.text: Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.
And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.

initial_triples.relationship: close eighth-day sacrificial service after consecration
initial_triples.rationale: From the eighth day the priests offer burnt and well-being offerings and God promises acceptance. Leviticus begins the eighth day's service with burnt offerings and a sacrifice of deliverance and promises the Lord's appearance. The common day and commencement of service connect them, with acceptance and appearance preserved as different statements.
initial_triples.source_text: From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”

target_units.text: And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.
And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,
and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.

initial_triples.relationship: related closures of distinct east-facing gates
initial_triples.rationale: This source describes the outer sanctuary gate facing east as shut. The later instruction concerns the inner-court east gate, shut on six working days but opened on Sabbaths and new moons. The locations and closure provisions are distinguished rather than treated as a contradiction about one gate.
initial_triples.source_text: He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the holy places, which faced east, and it was shut.

target_units.text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

initial_triples.relationship: close divine passage through the east-facing gate
initial_triples.rationale: The gate will remain shut because the Lord God of Israel will enter through it. The earlier vision describes the Lord's glory entering the house through the east-facing gate. The common route is explicit, while the source's future entry is not silently changed into the target's past action.
initial_triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “This gate will remain shut. It will not be opened, and no one will pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter through it. It will remain shut,

target_units.text: The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.

initial_triples.relationship: close correspondence of the ruler's gate entry and departure
initial_triples.rationale: The ruler enters by the gate's porch and goes out by his way, with eating bread before the Lord as the stated purpose here. The later instruction again makes the ruler enter by the porch and go out by the gate. The later unit does not separately repeat the meal.
initial_triples.source_text: for the ruler—he will sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He will enter by the way of the gate’s porch and go out by his way.”

target_units.text: When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

initial_triples.relationship: close glory filling the house and a human response before it
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel sees the Lord's house full of glory and falls on his face. At Solomon's dedication the Lord's glory fills the house and the priests cannot stand to minister. The sanctuary-filling presence is shared, while the particular bodily responses differ.
initial_triples.source_text: He brought me by the north gate opposite the house. I looked, and behold—the house of the Lord was full of glory. I fall on my face.

target_units.text: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the Lord’s glory filled the house.

initial_triples.relationship: close repeated demand for attentive eyes, ears and heart
initial_triples.rationale: God now commands Ezekiel to set his heart, see and hear the house's ordinances and entrances. The earlier guide gave the same threefold demand before showing the vision for Israel. The repetition marks attentive reception of the house's instruction without equating the two speakers.
initial_triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, set in your heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I speak with you concerning all the commands of the Lord’s house and all its ordinances. Set your heart on the house’s entrance, according to all its exits in all the holy places.

target_units.text: The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

initial_triples.relationship: close declaration of enough followed by a demand to end wrongdoing
initial_triples.rationale: God says Israel's lawless deeds must be enough. The following ruler instructions likewise say Enough to Israel's rulers and command removal of injustice and oppression. The shared declaration and demand are retained with the different groups addressed.
initial_triples.source_text: You will say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your lawless deeds be enough for you, house of Israel—

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.

initial_triples.relationship: related distinction between circumcision of flesh and heart
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel describes admitted foreigners as uncircumcised in both heart and flesh. initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel forbids an uncircumcised foreign son to enter the holy places, expressly naming heart and flesh. initial_triples.rationale: The Levites sprang away when Israel strayed and will receive their injustice. initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns these Levites gatekeeping, house ministry and slaughtering for the people. And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.

initial_triples.relationship: related harm and judgment associated with failed Levitical ministry
initial_triples.rationale: Ezekiel says their ministry before idols became a punishment of injustice for Israel, and God raised His hand against them. Malachi says the priests weakened many through the law and corrupted Levi's covenant; God says He made them despised and neglected. The harmful ministry and consequence connect them without adding an explicit oath to the source's raised hand.
initial_triples.source_text: Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became a punishment of injustice for the house of Israel, I raised My hand against them, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.

initial_triples.relationship: close assignment of Levitical custodial service with restricted approach
initial_triples.rationale: The ministers remain assigned to keep the house's duties and carry out its work, following the denial of priestly access. Exodus 20:22.text: And the Lord said to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel: ‘You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.

Exodus 20:23.text: You shall not make gods of silver for yourselves, nor shall you make gods of gold for yourselves.

Exodus 20:24.text: You shall make an altar of earth to Me and sacrifice on it your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices of deliverance, your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name My name; and I will come to you and bless you.

Exodus 20:25.text: But if you make Me an altar of stones, you shall not build with hewn stones; for you have laid your blade upon them, and they are defiled.

Exodus 20:26.text: You shall not go up by steps to My altar, lest you uncover your nakedness on it.’”

Exodus 25:1.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

Exodus 25:2.text: “Speak to the sons of Israel, and receive firstfruits for Me from everyone whose heart is willing. You shall receive My firstfruits.

Exodus 25:3.text: This is the firstfruit offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;

Exodus 25:4.text: blue, purple, double scarlet, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;

Exodus 25:5.text: rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and decay-resistant wood;

Exodus 25:7.text: sardius stones and stones for engraving, for the shoulder-piece and full-length robe.

Exodus 25:8.text: And you shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you.

Exodus 25:9.text: And you shall make it for Me according to all that I show you upon the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels; this is how you shall make it.

Exodus 25:23.text: You shall make a table of pure gold, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

Exodus 25:24.text: You shall make twisted gold mouldings around it.

Exodus 25:25.text: You shall make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a twisted moulding around the rim.

Exodus 25:26.text: You shall make four gold rings and put them at the four parts of its legs

Exodus 25:27.text: beneath the rim; and the rings shall be holders for the carrying poles, that the table may be borne with them.

Exodus 25:28.text: You shall make the carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried with them.

Exodus 25:29.text: You shall make its dishes, incense cups, libation vessels, and cups for pouring libations. You shall make them of pure gold.

Exodus 25:30.text: You shall place the bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.

Exodus 25:40.text: See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”

Exodus 26:30.text: You shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan shown to you on the mountain.

Exodus 26:31.text: You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, with cherubim, the work of a weaver.

Exodus 26:32.text: You shall place it on four posts of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals and four silver bases.

Exodus 26:33.text: And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

Exodus 26:34.text: You shall screen the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.

Exodus 26:35.text: You shall place the table outside the veil and the lampstand opposite it on the tabernacle’s south side; the table shall be on the north side.

Exodus 26:36.text: You shall make a screen of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.

Exodus 26:37.text: You shall make five posts for the curtain and overlay them with gold, with gold capitals, and cast five bronze bases for them.”

Exodus 27:1.text: “You shall make an altar of decay-resistant wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square and three cubits high.

Exodus 27:2.text: You shall make horns on its four corners, of one piece with it, and cover them with bronze.

Exodus 27:3.text: You shall make a rim for the altar, its cover, bowls, meat forks, and firepan. You shall make all its utensils of bronze.

Exodus 27:4.text: You shall make a bronze grating of network for it, with four bronze rings on its four sides.

Exodus 27:5.text: You shall place them beneath the altar’s grating, and the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.

Exodus 27:6.text: You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.

Exodus 27:7.text: You shall put the carrying poles through the rings, and they shall lie along the altar’s sides when it is carried.

Exodus 27:8.text: You shall make it hollow, of boards; as it was shown to you upon the mountain, so you shall make it.

Exodus 29:1.text: “This is what you shall do for them: consecrate them to serve Me as priests. Take one calf from the herd and two rams without blemish,

Exodus 29:2.text: unleavened loaves mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour.

Exodus 29:3.text: Put them on one basket and present them on the basket, together with the calf and the two rams.

Exodus 29:4.text: Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.

Exodus 29:5.text: Take the robes and clothe Aaron your brother with the full-length tunic, the shoulder-piece, and the oracle-piece. Fasten the oracle-piece to the shoulder-piece for him.

Exodus 29:6.text: Put the headband on his head and the holy plate on the headband.

Exodus 29:7.text: Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.

Exodus 29:8.text: Bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.

Exodus 29:9.text: Gird them with sashes and put turbans on them. The priesthood shall be theirs for Me for ever. You shall consecrate Aaron’s hands and the hands of his sons.

Exodus 29:10.text: Bring the calf to the doors of the Tent of Testimony. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the calf’s head before the Lord, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

Exodus 29:11.text: Slaughter the calf before the Lord at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

Exodus 29:12.text: Take some of the calf’s blood and put it on the altar’s horns with your finger. Pour all the remaining blood at the altar’s base.

Exodus 29:13.text: Take all the fat on the belly, the liver’s lobe, the two kidneys, and the fat on them, and place them on the altar.

Exodus 29:14.text: Burn the calf’s flesh, skin, and dung with fire outside the camp, for it is a sin offering.

Exodus 29:15.text: Take one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

Exodus 29:16.text: Slaughter it, take the blood, and pour it against the altar on every side.

Exodus 29:17.text: Divide the ram limb by limb, wash the entrails and feet with water, and place them on the pieces with the head.

Exodus 29:18.text: Offer the whole ram on the altar as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, a fragrant aroma; it is a sacrifice to the Lord.

Exodus 29:19.text: Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

Exodus 29:20.text: And you shall slaughter it, and take of its blood, and put it upon the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, and upon the extremity of his right hand and of his right foot, and upon the lobes of his sons’ right ears, and upon the extremities of their right hands and of their right feet.

Exodus 29:21.text: Take some blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his robe, and on his sons and their robes. He and his robe, and his sons and their robes, shall be holy. Pour the ram’s blood against the altar on every side.

Exodus 29:22.text: Take the ram’s fat, the fat covering its belly, the liver’s lobe, the two kidneys and their fat, and the right foreleg, for this is a consecration;

Exodus 29:23.text: also take one loaf made with oil and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread set before the Lord.

Exodus 29:24.text: Put all these on the hands of Aaron and his sons and set them apart as a dedicated portion before the Lord.

Exodus 29:25.text: Receive them from their hands and offer them on the altar of whole burnt offering as a fragrant aroma before the Lord, an offering to the Lord.

Exodus 29:26.text: Take the breast from Aaron’s ram of consecration and set it apart as a dedicated portion before the Lord. It shall be your portion.

Exodus 29:27.text: Consecrate the breast set apart and the foreleg of the contribution, which were set apart and taken from the ram of consecration for Aaron and his sons.

Exodus 29:28.text: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons by an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel; for it is a contribution, and shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, from their sacrifices of deliverance, a contribution to the Lord.

Exodus 29:29.text: Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in the garments and have their hands consecrated.

Exodus 29:30.text: The priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall wear them for seven days; he shall enter the Tent of Testimony to minister in the holy places.

Exodus 29:31.text: Take the ram of consecration and boil its flesh in a holy place.

Exodus 29:32.text: Aaron and his sons shall eat the ram’s flesh and the bread in the basket at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

Exodus 29:33.text: They shall eat the things by which they were sanctified, to consecrate their hands and sanctify them. An outsider shall not eat them, because they are holy.

Exodus 29:34.text: And if any of the flesh of the consecration sacrifice, or of the bread, remains until morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is a holy thing.

Exodus 29:35.text: Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.

Exodus 29:36.text: And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.

Exodus 29:37.text: For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.

Exodus 30:1.text: You shall make an incense altar of decay-resistant wood.

Exodus 30:2.text: It shall be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high, with horns of one piece with it.

Exodus 30:3.text: You shall overlay its grating, all its walls, and its horns with pure gold, and make a twisted gold rim around it.

Exodus 30:4.text: You shall make two rings of pure gold beneath its twisted rim, on its two flanks, on the two sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.

Exodus 30:5.text: You shall make the poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.

Exodus 30:6.text: You shall put it opposite the veil over the ark of the testimonies, where I will make Myself known to you.

Ezekiel 1:1.text: And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.

Ezekiel 1:2.text: On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—

Ezekiel 1:3.text: the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,

Ezekiel 1:5.text: And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,

Ezekiel 1:6.text: and each had four faces, and each had four wings.

Ezekiel 1:7.text: Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, with sparks like flashing bronze; and their wings were light.

Ezekiel 1:8.text: A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them

Ezekiel 1:9.text: did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.

Ezekiel 1:10.text: The likeness of their faces was a human face and a lion’s face on the right for all four, and a calf’s face on the left for all four, and an eagle’s face for all four.

Ezekiel 1:11.text: The wings of all four were stretched out above; each had two joined to one another, and two covered the top of their bodies.

Ezekiel 1:12.text: Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit was going, they went and did not turn.

Ezekiel 1:13.text: And amid the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, like the sight of torches whirling among the living creatures, and brightness of the fire; lightning came out of the fire.

Ezekiel 1:24.text: As they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water; when they stood, their wings came to rest.

Ezekiel 1:25.text: And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads.

Ezekiel 1:26.text: Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

Ezekiel 1:27.text: I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.

Ezekiel 1:28.text: Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.

Ezekiel 3:1.text: He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll, then go and speak to the sons of Israel.”

Ezekiel 3:2.text: I opened my mouth wide, and He fed me the scroll.

Ezekiel 3:3.text: He said to me, “Son of man, your mouth will eat, and your belly will be filled with this scroll that has been given to you.” I ate it, and in my mouth it became like sweet honey.

Ezekiel 3:4.text: He said to me, “Son of man, go, enter the house of Israel, and speak My words to them;

Ezekiel 3:22.text: The Lord’s hand came upon me, and He said to me, “Rise and go out to the plain, and you will be spoken to there.”

Ezekiel 3:23.text: I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.

Ezekiel 3:24.text: A spirit came upon me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said to me, “Go, be shut inside your house.

Ezekiel 3:25.text: And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them; you certainly will not go out from among them.

Ezekiel 3:26.text: I will bind your tongue, and you will become mute; you will not be a man rebuking them, for it is an embittering house.

Ezekiel 3:27.text: But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let the one who hears hear, and let the one who disobeys disobey,’ for it is an embittering house.”

Ezekiel 10:20.text: This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.

Ezekiel 10:21.text: Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.

Ezekiel 40:1.text: In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was captured, on that day the Lord’s hand came upon me, and He led me

Ezekiel 40:2.text: in a vision of God into Israel’s land and set me upon a very high mountain. Upon it, opposite, was something like a city’s structure.

Ezekiel 40:3.text: He brought me in there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like gleaming copper. In his hand were a builders’ cord and a measuring reed, and he stood at the gate.

Ezekiel 40:4.text: The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

Ezekiel 40:5.text: Behold, an enclosure surrounded the house outside. In the man’s hand was a reed measuring six cubits by the cubit and handbreadth. He measured the outer wall: its width equaled the reed, and its height equaled the reed.

Ezekiel 40:6.text: He entered the gate facing east by seven steps and measured the gate’s porch, equal to the reed,

Ezekiel 40:7.text: and the chamber, one reed long and one reed wide; the porch between the chambers was six cubits. The second chamber was one reed wide and one reed long, and the porch five cubits,

Ezekiel 40:8.text: and the third chamber was one reed wide and one reed long,

Ezekiel 40:9.text: and the gateway’s porch beside the gate’s porch was eight cubits, the jambs two cubits, and the gate’s porch was on the inside.

Ezekiel 40:10.text: The gate’s chambers stood opposite one another, three on this side and three on that side, one measurement for all three and one measurement for the porches on this side and that side.

Ezekiel 40:11.text: He measured the gateway door’s width, ten cubits, and the gateway’s breadth, thirteen cubits,

Ezekiel 40:12.text: with one additional cubit before the chambers on each side, and the chamber six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.

Ezekiel 40:13.text: He measured the gate from a chamber’s wall to a chamber’s wall, twenty-five cubits wide, gate opposite gate.

Ezekiel 40:14.text: The open court of the gate’s porch was sixty cubits, with twenty chambers around the gate.

Ezekiel 40:15.text: From the gate’s outer open court to the inner open court of the gate’s porch was fifty cubits.

Ezekiel 40:16.text: There were concealed windows upon the chambers and porches inside the courtyard gate all around, and likewise windows around the porches inward, and palm trees upon the porch on both sides.

Ezekiel 40:17.text: He brought me into the inner courtyard. Behold, there were chambers and colonnades around the courtyard, thirty chambers in the colonnades,

Ezekiel 40:18.text: and porticoes behind the gates, corresponding to the gates’ length—the lower colonnade.

Ezekiel 40:19.text: He measured the courtyard’s width from the outer gate’s open court inward to the open court of the gate facing outward, one hundred cubits, at the east-facing gate. He brought me north,

Ezekiel 40:20.text: and behold, a gate faced north in the outer courtyard. He measured its length and width.

Ezekiel 40:21.text: Its chambers, three on this side and three on that side, its jambs, porches and palm trees matched the east-facing gate’s measurements: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits broad.

Ezekiel 40:22.text: Its windows, porches and palm trees were like the east-facing gate. They went up it by seven steps, and its porches were on the inside.

Ezekiel 40:23.text: A gate in the inner courtyard faced the north gate, as with the east-facing gate. He measured the courtyard from gate to gate, one hundred cubits.

Ezekiel 40:24.text: He led me south, and behold, a gate faced south. He measured it, its chambers, jambs and porches according to these measurements.

Ezekiel 40:25.text: Its windows and porches all around were like the porch’s windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits broad.

Ezekiel 40:26.text: It had seven steps, with porches on the inside and palm trees upon its jambs, one on this side and one on that side.

Ezekiel 40:27.text: A gate stood opposite the gate of the inner courtyard toward the south. He measured the courtyard from gate to gate, a breadth of one hundred cubits toward the south.

Ezekiel 40:28.text: He brought me into the inner courtyard by the south-facing gate and measured the gate according to these measurements,

Ezekiel 40:29.text: with its chambers, jambs and porches according to these measurements. It and its porches had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits broad.

Ezekiel 40:31.text: The porches faced the outer courtyard, with palm trees upon the jambs and eight steps.

Ezekiel 40:32.text: He brought me into the east-facing gate and measured it according to these measurements,

Ezekiel 40:33.text: with its chambers, jambs and porches according to these measurements. It and its porches had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits broad.

Ezekiel 40:34.text: The porches faced the inner courtyard, with palm trees upon the jambs on this side and that side, and it had eight steps.

Ezekiel 40:35.text: He brought me into the north-facing gate and measured according to these measurements,

Ezekiel 40:36.text: with its chambers, jambs and porches. It and its porch had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits broad.

Ezekiel 40:37.text: Its porches faced the outer courtyard, with palm trees upon the jambs on this side and that side, and it had eight steps.

Ezekiel 40:38.text: Its chambers, doorframes and porches were at the gate—

Ezekiel 40:39.text: the second—with a drain, so that they may slaughter there the offerings for sin and for ignorance.

Ezekiel 40:40.text: Behind the burnt offerings’ channel at the north-facing gate were two tables toward the east; behind the second and the gate’s porch were two tables toward the east,

Ezekiel 40:41.text: four on this side and four on that side behind the gate. Upon them they will slaughter the victims, opposite the eight tables for victims.

Ezekiel 40:42.text: There were four hewn-stone tables for the burnt offerings, one and a half cubits wide, two and a half cubits long and one cubit high. Upon them they will place the implements with which they slaughter the burnt offerings and victims there.

Ezekiel 40:43.text: They will have a hewn ledge of one handbreadth inside all around, and coverings above the tables to shelter them from rain and dry heat.

Ezekiel 40:44.text: He brought me into the inner courtyard, and behold, two recessed chambers were in the inner courtyard: one behind the north-facing gate faced south, and one behind the south gate faced north.

Ezekiel 40:45.text: He said to me, ‘This recessed chamber facing south is for the priests who keep the house’s charge,

Ezekiel 40:46.text: and the recessed chamber facing north is for the priests who keep the altar’s charge. They are Zadok’s sons, who draw near to the Lord from Levi to minister to Him.’

Ezekiel 40:47.text: He measured the courtyard, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits broad on its four sides, and the altar before the house.

Ezekiel 40:48.text: He brought me into the house’s porch. He measured the porch’s jamb, five cubits broad on this side and five on that side; the doorway’s breadth was fourteen cubits, and the porch door’s side pieces three cubits on this side and three on that side.

Ezekiel 40:49.text: The porch was twenty cubits long and twelve cubits broad. They went up to it by ten steps, and there were pillars at the porch, one on this side and one on that side.
