Ezekiel 41:2.text: The gateway was ten cubits wide, with sidepieces of five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side. He measured its length, forty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits.

Ezekiel 41:3.text: He entered the inner court and measured the doorway’s jamb, two cubits; the doorway, six cubits; and the doorway’s sidepieces, seven cubits on this side and seven cubits on that side.

Ezekiel 41:4.text: He measured the length of the doors, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits, in front of the temple. He said, “This is the Most Holy Place.”

Ezekiel 41:5.text: He measured the house’s wall, six cubits, and the side chamber’s breadth, four cubits, all around.

Ezekiel 41:6.text: The side chambers stood chamber upon chamber, thirty and three, twice over. There was an interval in the house’s wall among the side chambers all around, so that those taking hold could see, and might not touch the house’s walls at all.

Ezekiel 41:7.text: The breadth of the upper side chambers followed the addition from the wall toward the upper part all around the house, so that it widened above and people could go up from the lower parts to the upper stories, and from the middle parts to the third stories.

Ezekiel 41:8.text: The house’s thrael rose all around; the interval of the side chambers equaled the reed, a space of six cubits.

Ezekiel 41:9.text: The outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits wide; the remaining spaces lay between the house’s side chambers—

Ezekiel 41:10.text: —and between the recessed chambers, with a breadth of twenty cubits, encircling the house all around.

Ezekiel 41:11.text: The doors of the recessed chambers opened onto the remaining area of the one door toward the north; the other door faced south. The opening of the remaining area was five cubits wide all around.

Ezekiel 41:12.text: The dividing structure opposite the remaining area toward the sea was seventy cubits. The dividing structure’s wall was five cubits in breadth all around, and its length was ninety cubits.

Ezekiel 41:13.text: He measured opposite the house, a length of a hundred cubits; the remaining spaces, dividing structures, and their walls were a hundred cubits long.

Ezekiel 41:14.text: The breadth in front of the house and the remaining spaces opposite was a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel 41:15.text: He measured the dividing structure opposite the remaining area behind that house, with the remaining spaces on both sides: a hundred cubits in length. The temple, the corners, and the outer porch—

Ezekiel 41:16.text: —were coffered. The windows were latticed, with openings for light around the three, so that one could look through. The house and the adjoining areas were covered with wood all around, as were the floor and the space from the floor to the windows; the windows opened in three ways for looking through.

Ezekiel 41:17.text: As far as the vicinity of the inner and outer parts, and over the whole wall all around, inside and outside,

Ezekiel 41:18.text: cherubim were carved, with palm trees between each cherub and the next. Each cherub had two faces:

Ezekiel 41:19.text: a human face toward the palm tree on this side and that side, and a lion’s face toward the palm tree on this side and that side. The whole house was carved all around,

Ezekiel 41:20.text: from the floor to the coffered ceiling, with the cherubim and palm trees carved.

Ezekiel 41:21.text: The holy place and the temple opened out in square forms. In front of the holy places was an appearance like the sight

Ezekiel 41:22.text: of a wooden altar, three cubits high, two cubits long, and two cubits broad. It had horns, and its base and its walls were wood. He said to me, “This is the table before the Lord.”

Ezekiel 41:23.text: The temple and the holy place had two doorways.

Ezekiel 41:24.text: The two pivoting doorways had two leaves: two leaves for the one and two leaves for the second door.

Ezekiel 41:25.text: Carving was on them, and on the temple’s doorways were cherubim and palm trees, matching the carving of the holy places. Fine timbers stood in front of the porch outside,

Ezekiel 41:26.text: with concealed windows. He measured on this side and that side toward the porch’s ceilings, and the house’s side chambers were joined together.

Ezekiel 42:1.text: He brought me out into the outer court toward the east, opposite the gate toward the north. He brought me in, and look—five recessed chambers adjoining the remaining area and adjoining the dividing structure toward the north.

Ezekiel 42:2.text: Their length toward the north extended a hundred cubits, and their breadth was fifty cubits.

Ezekiel 42:3.text: They were laid out like the gates of the inner court and like the colonnades of the outer court, arranged in facing rows: three porticoes.

Ezekiel 42:4.text: Opposite the recessed chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long; their doorways faced north.

Ezekiel 42:5.text: The upper walkways were likewise, because the colonnade projected from it, from the colonnade below, and so did the intervening space; thus a colonnade and an intervening space, and thus porticoes.

Ezekiel 42:6.text: For they were threefold and had no pillars like the pillars of the outer structures; therefore they projected beyond the lower and middle ones from the ground.

Ezekiel 42:7.text: There was an opening outside, like the recessed chambers of the outer court that faced opposite the recessed chambers toward the north, fifty cubits long.

Ezekiel 42:8.text: For the recessed chambers facing the outer court were fifty cubits long, and these faced those; the whole was a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel 42:9.text: The doors of these recessed chambers belonged to the entrance toward the east, through which one entered them from the outer court—

Ezekiel 42:10.text: —along the opening at the beginning of the walkway. And toward the south, facing the south, facing the remaining area and facing the dividing structure, were recessed chambers.

Ezekiel 42:11.text: The walkway in front of them followed the measurements of the recessed chambers toward the north—their length, their breadth, all their exits, all their turnings, their openings, and their doorways—

Ezekiel 42:12.text: —of the recessed chambers toward the south, and followed the doorways from the beginning of the walkway, toward an opening with an interval of a reed, and toward the east for entering through them.

Ezekiel 42:13.text: He said to me, “The recessed chambers toward the north and toward the south, facing the intervening spaces, are the chambers of the holy place. There the priests, the sons of Zadok who draw near to the Lord, will eat the most holy things. There they will place the most holy things—the offering, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance—for the place is holy.

Ezekiel 42:14.text: No one will enter there except the priests. They will not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that those who bring offerings may always be holy and may not touch the garments in which they minister, for they are holy. They will put on other garments whenever they come into contact with the people.”

Ezekiel 42:15.text: The measurement of the house inside was completed. He brought me out by the gate facing east and measured the plan of the house all around in its arrangement.

Ezekiel 42:16.text: He stood behind the gate facing east and measured five hundred with the measuring reed.

Ezekiel 42:17.text: He turned toward the north and measured the north-facing side: five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.

Ezekiel 42:18.text: He turned toward the sea and measured the sea-facing side: five hundred with the measuring reed.

Ezekiel 42:19.text: He turned toward the south and measured opposite the south: five hundred with the measuring reed.

Ezekiel 42:20.text: The four sides were measured with the same reed. He laid it out, with their enclosure all around: five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to distinguish between the holy areas and the forewall in the arrangement of the house.

Ezekiel 43:1.text: He led me to the gate facing east and brought me out.

Ezekiel 43:2.text: Look—the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way of the gate facing east. The sound of the camp was like the sound of many redoubling their sound, and the earth flashed like radiance from the glory all around.

Ezekiel 43:3.text: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I was entering to anoint the city; and the vision of the chariot I saw was like the vision I had seen by the River Chobar. I fall on my face.

Ezekiel 43:4.text: The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.

Ezekiel 43:5.text: A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.

Ezekiel 43:6.text: I stood, and look—a voice from the house, speaking to me, while the man stood next to me.

Ezekiel 43:7.text: He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man, the place of My throne and the place of the footprints of My feet, where My name will dwell among the house of Israel for ever? The house of Israel will no longer profane My holy name, neither they nor their rulers, by their prostitution and by the murders of the rulers among them—

Ezekiel 43:8.text: —when they set My vestibule among their vestibules and My doorposts next to their doorposts, and placed My wall as adjoining Me and them. They profaned My holy name by the lawless deeds they practiced, and I wiped them out in My wrath and in slaughter.

Ezekiel 43:9.text: Now let them drive their prostitution and the murders of their rulers away from Me, and I will dwell among them for ever.

Ezekiel 43:10.text: You, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, and they will cease from their sins. Show its appearance and its arrangement—

Ezekiel 43:11.text: —and they will receive their punishment for everything they have done. You will draw the house, its exits, and its structure; make known to them all its commands and all its ordinances, and draw them before them. They will keep all My judgments and all My commands and carry them out,

Ezekiel 43:12.text: together with the drawing of the house on the mountain’s summit: all its boundaries all around are most holy.”

Ezekiel 43:13.text: These are the altar’s measurements in a cubit consisting of a cubit and a handbreadth: a hollow one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a ledge along its edge all around of a span. This was the altar’s height:

Ezekiel 43:14.text: from the depth at the beginning of its hollow to the large lower place of atonement, two cubits, with a breadth of a cubit; and from the small place of atonement to the large place of atonement, four cubits, with a breadth of a cubit.

Ezekiel 43:15.text: The Ariel was four cubits, and from the Ariel upward above the horns was a cubit.

Ezekiel 43:16.text: The Ariel was twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.

Ezekiel 43:17.text: The place of atonement was fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its surrounding ledge ran all around it at half a cubit, and its surrounding band was a cubit all around. Its steps faced east.

Ezekiel 43:18.text: He said to me, “Son of man, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: These are the altar’s commands on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and pouring blood against it.

Ezekiel 43:19.text: You will give the Levitical priests who are of Zadok’s offspring and draw near to Me to minister to Me, says the Lord God, a calf from the cattle as an offering for sin.

Ezekiel 43:20.text: They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.

Ezekiel 43:21.text: They will take the calf for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the separated area of the house, outside the holy places.

Ezekiel 43:22.text: On the second day they will take two unblemished goat kids for sin, and they will make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the calf.

Ezekiel 43:23.text: After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.

Ezekiel 43:24.text: You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.

Ezekiel 43:25.text: For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—

Ezekiel 43:26.text: —for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.

Ezekiel 43:27.text: From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”

Ezekiel 44:1.text: He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the holy places, which faced east, and it was shut.

Ezekiel 44:2.text: The Lord said to me, “This gate will remain shut. It will not be opened, and no one will pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter through it. It will remain shut,

Ezekiel 44:3.text: for the ruler—he will sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He will enter by the way of the gate’s porch and go out by his way.”

Ezekiel 44:4.text: He brought me by the north gate opposite the house. I looked, and behold—the house of the Lord was full of glory. I fall on my face.

Ezekiel 44:5.text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, set in your heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I speak with you concerning all the commands of the Lord’s house and all its ordinances. Set your heart on the house’s entrance, according to all its exits in all the holy places.

Ezekiel 44:6.text: You will say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your lawless deeds be enough for you, house of Israel—

Ezekiel 44:7.text: —your bringing in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My holy places. They profaned them while you offered bread, fat, and blood, and you transgressed My covenant in all your lawless deeds.

Ezekiel 44:8.text: You arranged for the keeping of duties in My holy places.

Ezekiel 44:9.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreign son uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh will enter My holy places, among all the foreign sons who are in the midst of the house of Israel,

Ezekiel 44:10.text: except the Levites, who sprang away from Me when Israel strayed from Me after their reflections; they will receive their injustice—

Ezekiel 44:11.text: —and will serve in My holy places as gatekeepers at the house’s gates and as ministers to the house. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and stand before the people to serve them.

Ezekiel 44:12.text: Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became a punishment of injustice for the house of Israel, I raised My hand against them, says the Lord God.

Ezekiel 44:13.text: They will not draw near to Me to serve Me as priests, nor approach the holy things of the sons of Israel, nor My most holy things. They will receive their dishonor in the straying by which they strayed.

Ezekiel 44:14.text: They will assign them to keep the duties of the house, for all its works and everything they may do.

Ezekiel 44:15.text: The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the duties of My holy places when the house of Israel strayed from Me, will approach Me to minister to Me. They will stand before Me to offer sacrifice, fat, and blood to Me, says the Lord God.

Ezekiel 44:16.text: They will enter My holy places and approach My table to minister to Me, and they will keep My duties.

Ezekiel 44:17.text: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they will put on linen robes. They will not wear woolen things when they minister from the gate of the inner court.

Ezekiel 44:18.text: They will have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers on their hips, and they will not bind their clothing tightly.

Ezekiel 44:19.text: When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the robes in which they minister, place them in the recessed chambers of the holy places, and put on other robes. They will certainly not sanctify the people with their robes.

Ezekiel 44:20.text: They will not shave their heads or strip away their hair; they will certainly cover their heads.

Ezekiel 44:21.text: No priest will drink wine when they enter the inner court.

Ezekiel 44:22.text: They will not take a widow or a woman who has been sent away as a wife, but a virgin of Israel’s offspring; if she is a priest’s widow, they may take her.

Ezekiel 44:23.text: They will teach My people the difference between holy and profane, and make known to them the difference between unclean and clean.

Ezekiel 44:24.text: In a case involving blood they will stand to decide. They will uphold My judgments and judge My decisions; they will keep My ordinances and My commands at all My festivals, and sanctify My Sabbaths.

Ezekiel 44:25.text: They will not approach a human corpse so as to be defiled, except that a priest may be defiled for his father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or sister who has not belonged to a husband.

Ezekiel 44:26.text: After he has been cleansed, one will count seven days for him.

Ezekiel 44:27.text: On whatever day they enter the inner court to minister in the holy place, they will bring an atonement offering, says the Lord God.

Ezekiel 44:28.text: This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. No possession will be given them among the sons of Israel, because I am their possession.

Ezekiel 44:29.text: They will eat the sacrifices, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance. Everything set apart in Israel will belong to them.

Ezekiel 44:30.text: The firstfruits of everything, the firstborn of everything, and all the contributions from all your firstfruits will belong to the priests. You will give your first produce to the priest, to place your blessings upon your houses.

Ezekiel 44:31.text: The priests will not eat anything that has died of itself or has been taken by a beast, whether from the birds or from the livestock.”

Ezekiel 45:1.text: “When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.

Ezekiel 45:2.text: From this, a square of five hundred by five hundred will be for a sanctuary, with an interval of fifty cubits all around it.

Ezekiel 45:3.text: From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.

Ezekiel 45:4.text: It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.

Ezekiel 45:5.text: An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad will belong to the Levites who minister to the house, as their possession, with cities in which to dwell.

Ezekiel 45:6.text: You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

Ezekiel 45:7.text: The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.

Ezekiel 45:8.text: It will be his possession in Israel. Israel’s rulers will no longer oppress My people, and the house of Israel will inherit the land according to their tribes.

Ezekiel 45:9.text: Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.

Ezekiel 46:1.text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

Ezekiel 46:2.text: The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.

Ezekiel 46:3.text: The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.

Ezekiel 46:4.text: The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,

Ezekiel 46:5.text: with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.

Ezekiel 46:6.text: On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.

Ezekiel 46:7.text: A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

Ezekiel 46:8.text: When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

Ezekiel 46:9.text: When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.

Ezekiel 46:10.text: The ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they go out, he will go out.

Ezekiel 46:11.text: At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

Ezekiel 46:12.text: If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.

Ezekiel 46:19.text: He brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the north-facing recessed chamber of the priests’ holy places. Look—there was a separated place there.

Ezekiel 46:20.text: He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the offerings for ignorance and for sin, and there bake the entire grain offering, so as not to carry it out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”

Ezekiel 46:21.text: He brought me out into the outer court and led me around its four sides. Look—a court at one side of the court, and a court at another side of the court!

Ezekiel 46:22.text: At the four sides of the court was a small court, forty cubits long and thirty cubits broad; the four had one measure.

Ezekiel 46:23.text: There were recessed chambers all around them, around the four, with kitchens made underneath the recessed chambers all around.

Ezekiel 46:24.text: He said to me, “These are the kitchen houses, where those ministering to the house will boil the people’s sacrificial animals.”

Isaiah 2:1.text: The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.

Isaiah 2:2.text: In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

Isaiah 2:3.text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

Isaiah 2:4.text: He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.

Isaiah 2:5.text: And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!

Isaiah 4:1.text: Seven women will take hold of one man, saying, “We will eat our own bread and put on our own clothes; only let your name be called over us. Take away our disgrace!”

Isaiah 4:2.text: On that day God will shine out in counsel with glory upon the earth, to exalt and glorify what remains of Israel,

Isaiah 4:3.text: and those remaining in Zion and left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all those recorded for life in Jerusalem,

Isaiah 4:4.text: because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

Isaiah 4:5.text: He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.

Isaiah 4:6.text: It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.

Isaiah 52:1.text: Awake, awake, Zion! Clothe yourself with your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, holy city. No uncircumcised and unclean person will pass through you again.

Isaiah 52:2.text: Shake off the dust and rise; sit, Jerusalem. Strip off the bond around your neck, captive daughter Zion.

Jeremiah 1:1.text: The word of God that came upon Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests, who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,

Jeremiah 1:2.text: which became God’s word to him in the days of Josiah son of Amos, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

Jeremiah 1:3.text: It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem’s captivity in the fifth month.

Jeremiah 1:4.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Jeremiah 9:24.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit all who have been circumcised in their foreskins:

Jeremiah 9:25.text: Egypt and Judea and Edom and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab and everyone who clips the hair around his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all Israel’s house are uncircumcised in their hearts.

Leviticus 2:11.text: You shall not make with leaven any sacrifice which you bring unto the Lord; for you shall bring neither any leaven nor any honey from it as an offering unto the Lord.

Leviticus 2:12.text: As a gift of firstfruits you shall bring them unto the Lord; but it shall not be brought up upon the altar for a sweet savour unto the Lord.

Leviticus 2:13.text: And every gift of your sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of the Lord cease from your sacrifices; with every gift of yours you shall bring salt unto the Lord your God.

Leviticus 4:22.text: And if the ruler sins, and unintentionally does any of the things which the commandments of the Lord their God forbid, and sins and commits an offence,

Leviticus 4:23.text: and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring as his gift an unblemished male young goat from the goats.

Leviticus 4:24.text: And he shall lay his hand upon the young goat’s head; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

Leviticus 4:25.text: And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.

Leviticus 4:26.text: And he shall offer up all its fat upon the altar, as the fat of a sacrifice of deliverance. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

Leviticus 6:1.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:2.text: Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of whole burning. The whole burnt offering shall remain upon its burning place upon the altar all night until morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it, and shall not be quenched.

Leviticus 6:3.text: And the priest shall put on a linen tunic, and he shall put linen undergarments about his body; and he shall remove from the altar the burnt remains of the whole burning which the fire has consumed, and place them beside the altar.

Leviticus 6:4.text: And he shall take off his robe, and put on another robe, and carry the burnt remains outside the camp unto a clean place.

Leviticus 6:5.text: And the fire upon the altar shall burn from it, and shall not be quenched; and the priest shall burn wood upon it in the morning, and pile the whole burnt offering upon it, and place upon it the fat of the offering of deliverance.

Leviticus 6:6.text: And a fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be quenched.

Leviticus 6:7.text: This is the law of the sacrifice which the sons of Aaron shall bring before the Lord, opposite the altar.

Leviticus 6:8.text: And he shall take a handful from the fine flour of the sacrifice, with its oil and the frankincense upon the sacrifice, and offer it up upon the altar as an offering: a sweet savour, its memorial portion unto the Lord.

Leviticus 6:9.text: But Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Testimony.

Leviticus 6:10.text: It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it unto them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, as the offering for sin and the guilt offering.

Leviticus 6:11.text: Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations, from the offerings of the Lord. Whosoever touches them shall be sanctified.

Leviticus 6:12.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:13.text: This is the gift of Aaron and his sons which they shall bring unto the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour as a continual sacrifice, half in the morning and half in the evening.

Leviticus 6:14.text: It shall be made upon a griddle with oil; he shall bring it mixed, in rolled pieces, a sacrifice of fragments, a sacrifice for a sweet savour unto the Lord.

Leviticus 6:15.text: The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his stead shall prepare it. It is an everlasting law; it shall all be fully performed.

Leviticus 6:16.text: And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned, and shall not be eaten.

Leviticus 6:17.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:18.text: Speak unto Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the offerings for sin before the Lord; they are most holy.

Leviticus 6:19.text: The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.

Leviticus 6:20.text: Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.

Leviticus 6:21.text: And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water.

Leviticus 6:22.text: Every male among the priests shall eat them; they are most holy unto the Lord.

Leviticus 6:23.text: And none of the offerings for sin whose blood is brought into the Tent of Testimony to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; they shall be burned with fire.

Leviticus 8:1.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 8:2.text: Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.

Leviticus 8:3.text: And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.

Leviticus 8:4.text: And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.

Leviticus 8:5.text: And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.

Leviticus 8:6.text: And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

Leviticus 8:7.text: And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.

Leviticus 8:8.text: And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.

Leviticus 8:9.text: And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.

Leviticus 8:10.text: And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

Leviticus 8:11.text: and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.

Leviticus 8:12.text: And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.

Leviticus 8:13.text: And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.

Leviticus 8:14.text: And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

Leviticus 8:15.text: And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.

Leviticus 8:31.text: And Moses said unto Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it, and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as I have been directed, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them.

Leviticus 8:32.text: And what remains of the flesh and loaves shall be burned up with fire.

Leviticus 8:33.text: And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for he shall consecrate your hands for seven days.

Leviticus 8:34.text: As he has done this day, the Lord commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.

Leviticus 8:35.text: And you shall remain at the door of the Tent of Testimony seven days, day and night; you shall keep the charges of the Lord, so that you do not die, for thus the Lord God commanded me.

Leviticus 8:36.text: And Aaron and his sons did all the things the Lord directed Moses.

Leviticus 9:1.text: And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.

Leviticus 9:2.text: And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.

Leviticus 9:3.text: And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,

Leviticus 9:4.text: and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.

Leviticus 10:8.text: And the Lord spoke unto Aaron, saying:

Leviticus 10:9.text: You shall drink no wine or strong drink, you and your sons with you, when you enter the Tent of Testimony, or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die: an everlasting statute throughout your generations,

Leviticus 10:10.text: to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.

Leviticus 10:11.text: And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

Leviticus 16:1.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses after Aaron’s two sons died when they presented strange fire before the Lord and died.

Leviticus 16:2.text: And the Lord said unto Moses: Speak unto Aaron your brother, and let him not enter at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the propitiatory cover which is upon the ark of testimony, so that he does not die; for I will appear in a cloud above the propitiatory cover.

Leviticus 16:3.text: In this way Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a calf from the cattle for sin and a ram for a whole burnt offering.

Leviticus 16:4.text: And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.

Leviticus 16:5.text: And from the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male young goats from the goats for sin and one ram for a whole burnt offering.

Leviticus 16:6.text: And Aaron shall present the calf for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his house.

Leviticus 21:1.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say unto them: They shall not be defiled for dead persons among their nation,

Leviticus 21:2.text: except for their nearest household kin: father, mother, sons, daughters, and brother;

Leviticus 21:3.text: and for a virgin sister near to him who has not been given to a man—for these he may defile himself.

Leviticus 21:4.text: He shall not suddenly defile himself among his people, so as to profane himself.

Leviticus 21:5.text: And you shall not shave a bald patch on your head for a dead person. They shall not shave the face of their beard or cut incisions in their flesh.

Leviticus 21:6.text: They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they present the Lord’s sacrifices, the gifts of their God; therefore they shall be holy.

Leviticus 21:7.text: They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, nor a woman expelled by her husband, for the priest is holy unto the Lord his God.

Leviticus 21:8.text: And he shall sanctify him; this man presents the gifts of the Lord your God. He shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord who sanctifies them.

Leviticus 21:9.text: And if a priest’s daughter is profaned by prostituting herself, she profanes her father’s name. She shall be burned with fire.

Leviticus 21:10.text: And the high priest among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured, and who has been consecrated to put on the garments, shall not remove his turban, neither shall he rend his garments;

Leviticus 21:11.text: and he shall not enter where there is any dead person; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or mother.

Leviticus 21:12.text: And he shall not leave the holy precincts or profane what is consecrated to his God, for the holy anointing oil of God is upon him. I am the Lord.

Leviticus 21:13.text: He shall take a virgin wife from his own kin.

Leviticus 21:14.text: A widow, an expelled woman, a profaned woman, or a prostitute—these he shall not take. He shall take as his wife only a virgin from his own kin.

Leviticus 21:15.text: And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.

Leviticus 22:1.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Leviticus 22:2.text: Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.

Leviticus 22:3.text: Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 22:4.text: And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,

Leviticus 22:5.text: or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.

Leviticus 22:6.text: The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;

Leviticus 22:7.text: and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.

Leviticus 22:8.text: He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.

Leviticus 22:9.text: And they shall keep My requirements, so that they do not incur sin through them and die through them if they profane them. I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.

Malachi 2:1.text: “And now this command is for you, priests.

Malachi 2:2.text: If you do not listen and do not take it into your hearts to give glory to My name,” says the Lord Almighty, “I will send out the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessing, and I will curse it. I will scatter your blessing, and it will not be among you, because you do not take it into your hearts.

Malachi 2:3.text: Look, I am setting apart the shoulder for you, and I will scatter the stomach on your faces, the stomach of your festivals, and I will take you to the same place.

Malachi 2:4.text: You will recognize that I have sent out this command to you, so that My covenant might be with the Levites,” says the Lord Almighty.

Malachi 2:5.text: “My covenant with him was of life and peace, and I gave it to him in fear, to fear Me and to shrink back before My name.

Malachi 2:6.text: A law of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips. Directing his way in peace, he walked with Me and turned many back from injustice.

Malachi 2:7.text: For a priest’s lips will guard knowledge, and people will seek law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty.

Malachi 2:8.text: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.

Malachi 2:9.text: “And I have made you despised and neglected among all the nations, because you did not guard My ways but showed partiality in the law.”

Numbers 7:89.text: When Moses entered the Tent of Testimony to speak with Him, he heard the voice of the Lord speaking to him from above the propitiatory cover on the ark of Testimony, between the two cherubim. He spoke to him.

Numbers 18:1.text: And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.

Numbers 18:2.text: And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 18:3.text: And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.

Numbers 18:4.text: And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.

Numbers 18:5.text: And you shall keep the charges of the holy things and the charges of the altar, and there shall be no wrath among the sons of Israel.

Numbers 18:6.text: And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 18:7.text: And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

Numbers 18:8.text: And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

Numbers 18:9.text: And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.

Numbers 18:10.text: You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

Numbers 18:11.text: And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.

Numbers 18:12.text: Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.

Numbers 18:13.text: All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.

Numbers 18:14.text: Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

Numbers 18:15.text: And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.

Numbers 18:16.text: And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

Numbers 18:17.text: But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.

Numbers 18:18.text: And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Numbers 18:19.text: Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.

Numbers 18:20.text: And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.

Numbers 18:21.text: And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 18:22.text: And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

Numbers 18:23.text: And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

Numbers 18:24.text: For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.

Numbers 19:11.text: Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.

Numbers 19:12.text: That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Numbers 19:13.text: Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.

Numbers 19:14.text: And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.

Numbers 19:15.text: And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.

Numbers 19:16.text: And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.

Numbers 19:17.text: And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

Numbers 19:18.text: And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

Numbers 19:19.text: And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

Zechariah 1:1.text: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:

Zechariah 1:2.text: “The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger.

Zechariah 1:3.text: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.

Zechariah 1:4.text: Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.

Zechariah 1:5.text: Your fathers—where are they? And the prophets—surely they will not live forever?

Zechariah 1:6.text: Yet receive My words and My ordinances, all that I, in My Spirit, command My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers.” And they answered and said, “As the Lord Almighty has arrayed Himself to act according to your ways and practices, so He acted toward you.”

Zechariah 1:7.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month—which is the month Sabat—in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:

Zechariah 1:8.text: I saw in the night: look, a man mounted on a flame-red horse! He stood between the two shaded mountains, and behind him were flame-red, gray, dappled and white horses.

Zechariah 2:1.text: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, four horns!

Zechariah 2:2.text: I said to the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel.”

Zechariah 2:3.text: The Lord showed me four craftsmen.

Zechariah 2:4.text: I said, “What are these coming to do?” He said to me, “These horns that scattered Judah also shattered Israel, and none of them lifted a head. These entered to sharpen them for their hands—the four horns, the nations lifting a horn against the Lord’s land to scatter it.”

Zechariah 2:5.text: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, a man with a land-measuring cord in his hand!

Zechariah 2:6.text: I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long.”

Zechariah 2:7.text: Look, the angel speaking within me was standing, and another angel was going out to meet him,

Zechariah 2:8.text: and said to him, “Run and speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited fruitfully because of the multitude of people and animals within her.

Zechariah 2:9.text: I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”
